purpose: Which solvents form explosive peroxides, with each list's class. Replaces the 5-row hand-typed table.

classes.A: severe peroxide hazard on storage without concentration
classes.D: may form peroxides but cannot clearly be placed in A-C
classes.disputed: the lists disagree and only one list gives the class
classes.not listed: in none of these lists; no list publishes negatives, so this is not 'does not form peroxides'

class_rule: A name in a list is one vote and a class entry matched by structure (vinyl ethers, other secondary alcohols, glycol ether acetates, dioxanes) half a vote; ties go to Prudent Practices or Illinois; a class only VUMC gives is marked disputed
chem21_rule: The CHEM21 guide's +1 Safety point follows the EU peroxide code EUH019 (harmonized); the lab classes do not set it. An ether with no EU status is 'peroxide point not assessed'.

sources.use: NRC 2011 Prudent Practices, ch. 4, Table 4.8 (classes A-C, sources Jackson 1970 and Kelly 1996) and Table 4.9
harmonized entries carrying EUH019 (may form explosive peroxides): 13 entries
